# SkyOS

> SkyOS is one memory for Claude, ChatGPT and Codex. It turns what you decide in your AI chats into short, dated notes that all three apps read, so you don't re-explain your project in every chat.

## What it does

- Connects to Claude, ChatGPT and Codex as an MCP server. Every connected app reads and saves the same notes.
- Notes keep the exact numbers, names and reasons you gave, not a summary. Each note is dated, and relative dates ("next Friday") are saved as real ones.
- The AI is told today's date and when the memory was started. When a note older than a month holds a number or a status, it says when it was true ("as of 18 August, …") instead of presenting it as current. It asks whether such a fact still holds only before it goes into something public, and asks once when a deadline in a note has passed with no word on how it went.
- Each new chat starts its own memory, so projects stay apart. To pick up in another chat, in any connected app, say "continue my last chat", or "continue" and the memory's name: the chat carries on with the same notes and the last few messages.
- Notes are rewritten when you change your mind. You can read, edit, export and delete them on the dashboard at app.skyos.ink.
- SkyOS keeps only the last five exchanges of each chat, deleted after 30 quiet days. Everything older exists only as notes.

## Pricing

- Free during the beta, up to 1,000 saved messages a month.
- Claude and Codex work on free plans; ChatGPT needs a paid plan.
